title: Telecom store rep
tagline: Learn to match phone and internet plans to each shopper and close on the spot.
you_are: a retail telecom consultant in a carrier store
setting: A branded carrier store where shoppers walk in to browse devices, compare plans or fix account issues.

scenarios.label: First walk in browser
scenarios.desc: Greet a casual shopper, uncover needs and steer them to a plan and device today.
scenarios.setup: You are a retail telecom consultant. A shopper pauses at the feature wall, glances at the new phones and mutters just looking thanks.
scenarios.objective: Book a plan and device before they leave the store.

scenarios.label: Switcher needing boss approval
scenarios.desc: Handle a small-business owner who likes the offer but must check with a partner before committing.
scenarios.setup: You are a retail telecom consultant. The shopper nods at the business bundle price then says I will have to speak to my boss about this.
scenarios.skills: Objection handling, value framing, next-step commitment
scenarios.objective: Set a firm follow-up time and send a comparison sheet while they are in store.

scenarios.label: Loyalist retention upgrade
scenarios.desc: Keep a long-time customer from leaving by solving a coverage complaint and upgrading their plan.
scenarios.setup: You are a retail telecom consultant. The shopper sets their bill on the counter and states flatly my signal still drops in my basement office so I am leaving.
scenarios.objective: Resolve the coverage issue and lock in a higher-value plan today.

buyers.angle: Concerned about cost and time investment for new service.
Asks many technical questions and resists rushed pitches.
Keeps checking watch and says they need to call partner.
Refuses to budge unless extra features are added at no cost.
Uses competitor pricing as leverage to demand lower monthly rate.

objections: I’ll have to speak to my boss about this
It’s not a good time right now
I already have a plan with another provider
Your price is higher than the other one
Do you have a promotion that’s not listed online?
I need to check with my team before deciding

rubric.label: Needs discovery
rubric.what: Ask open-ended questions that reveal usage, budget and pain points before any recommendation.

rubric.label: Plan matching
rubric.what: Recommend the exact plan and device that fit the uncovered needs without overselling.

rubric.label: Objection handling
rubric.what: Acknowledge the concern, ask a targeted follow-up question and keep the conversation moving forward.

rubric.label: Value framing
rubric.what: Translate features into personal benefits that outweigh the shopper’s hesitation.

rubric.label: Compliance accuracy
rubric.what: State prices, fees, contract terms and coverage limits exactly as the carrier publishes them.

rubric.label: Next step commitment
rubric.what: Secure a concrete action such as activation, scheduled call or signed agreement before the shopper leaves.

pitfalls: Quoting a promotional price without the required autopay or trade-in conditions.
Promising coverage in a specific building area the carrier map does not guarantee.
Letting a shopper walk away with only a brochure and no agreed follow-up.
line: Selling phone and internet plans in a retail store

research.text: Common customer objections when selling phone and internet plans in a retail store include prospects wanting to email information ("Can you email this over?"), wanting to speak to their boss ("I’ll have to speak to my boss about this."), and wanting to get off the phone ("Just send me some info"). To handle these objections, ask open-ended questions to evaluate their needs, offer to send information immediately while asking a targeted question, and use the 4 P’s Framework to address unexpected objections. Additionally, if prospects claim it’s not a good time, focus on creating value and understanding their specific needs. If they already have a solution, explore if it’s a budget or priority issue. The sources do not provide a definitive answer to all objections but suggest these strategies.
